title: Live reasoning: three layouts
question: Each layout plays back the same real Pi turn: the claude-opus-5-5 lead from 6 Nov at 12:26, with its recorded thinking, its exact bash commands and their real output. The newest thought types in at the live edge. Nothing is invented, and the old inline/dock/timeline mockups are not reused. Pick a layout, or say what is wrong with all three. “Build this” records a design preference only.

options.label: One stream, like Pi
options.thesis: The conversation is the Pi session: your message, then the agent's thinking (italic) and tool calls ($ command, output tail) in recorded order, then the reply. A finished turn folds its work into one line above the reply. Inbox and agents share the left column, so the stream gets about 1000px.
options.viewport: 1600 × 1000, live edge; also 1280 × 800, 900 × 800, and a history capture with the earlier turn opened.
options.risk: Long Claude reasoning pushes earlier replies far up; you rely on the fold line to find them.

options.label: Dialogue beside Work
options.thesis: The left pane holds only what you and the agent said to each other. The right pane is the agent's live work: thinking and tool calls streaming, with the current todo in its header. Replies never get buried under tool output.
options.viewport: 1600 × 1000 and 1280 × 800 side by side; at 900 × 800, Dialogue and Work become two tabs.
options.risk: Two scroll regions to read. At narrow widths you switch tabs to see the work.

options.label: Focus on one agent
options.thesis: The agents list leaves the left side. Working agents become a row of cards across the top, each with its newest thought or command. The inbox keeps its own column on the left. The chosen agent's stream fills the width below.
options.viewport: 1600 × 1000, 1280 × 800 and 900 × 800; todos sit in a right margin from 1400px.
options.risk: With many agents, the card row scrolls sideways, and the full list is one click away.
